metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (/compact is a live-confirmed, real slash command with dedicated CLI flags and a first-class wire-protocol RPC + item kind). daemon_capability: full, but LOW-CONFIDENCE/PROVISIONAL -- grounded in muse's existing generic, content-agnostic run-boundary mechanism (already daemon=full for 12/12 core scenarios), but with a NAMED, precedent-based risk (copilot's own /compact needed a dedicated parser arm because its compaction call emitted no ordinary turn-start marker) that muse's compaction may behave the same way and simply never enter `working` at all. driver_capability: ready (slash step already implemented and proven live in 2-5).

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes (confidence high)
daemon_capability: full (confidence LOW -- provisional, unconfirmed by any live emission)
driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

### agent_supports: yes

muse ships a real, user-invocable `/compact` slash command AND CLI-level compaction controls, confirmed directly from the installed binary (`strings ~/.local/bin/muse-bin-1.2.1-R2847.1`), not vendor docs:

- The TUI's command table lists `/compact` with help text `"Summarize the conversation to free up context [transcript|trajectory]"`, alongside every other slash command (`/clear`, `/model`, `/resume`, etc.).
- `muse exec --help` exposes top-level flags `--context-compaction-strategy <ID>`, `--context-compaction-soft-threshold <FRAC>`, and `--context-compaction-hard-threshold <FRAC>` -- compaction is a first-class, independently configurable CLI surface, not an undocumented side effect.
- The wire protocol schema (`msp.schema.json`, recovered from a live install at `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../muse-schema/msp.schema.json`) defines a dedicated `session/compact` RPC (`SessionCompactParams`/`SessionCompactResult`) explicitly described as "the `/compact` gesture", plus `CompactionOutcome` (`compacted|noop|failed|cancelled`) and `CompactionTrigger` (`manual|auto`) enums.
- `compaction` is one of the schema's 9 v1 `ItemKind` values (`userMessage`, `agentMessage`, `reasoning`, `toolCall`, `userShell`, `subagent`, `workflow`, `reminderChild`, `compaction`) -- a first-class transcript item type on par with tool calls and messages, carrying dedicated fields `outcome`, `trigger`, `tokensBefore`, `tokensAfter`, `strategyId`.

This is multi-source, live-surface evidence (binary strings + wire schema), not a doc guess -- confidence high.

### daemon_capability: full, but provisional (confidence 0.55)

**The optimistic case.** muse's `working`/`ready` state derivation is driven ENTIRELY by a generic, content-agnostic boundary: `payload_type:"runtime.session"` -> `payload.kind:"run"` -> `event.kind:"started"|"terminal"` (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:160-161`, `306-365`). `parseRunStarted`/`parseRunTerminal` have NO special-casing on what kind of work a run performs -- ANY run, including one that executes compaction's summarization call, would produce the visible `ready->working->ready` arc through the SAME mechanism already confirmed `daemon=full` for the adapter's 12/12 core scenarios. Any unrecognized compaction-specific sub-event (e.g. a future `context_compaction_installed`) falls to the parser's existing `default: ev.Skip=true` branch (parser.go:288-302) -- harmless bookkeeping, not a break in the state arc. This mirrors claudecode's own reference verdict for the identical scenario (`replaydata/agents/claudecode/scenarios/2-12_context-compaction/metadata.json`): `daemon=full` via the same generic long-working-turn mechanism, with the domain's compaction-labeling field being separately unused/dead code -- immaterial because the scenario's acceptance_criteria assert only the visible state arc, never a compaction-specific label.

**The named risk (why confidence is 0.55, not 0.85).** This optimism rests on an UNCONFIRMED assumption: that muse's `/compact` execution actually routes through the same `kind:"run"`/`started` record every ordinary turn uses. There is a DIRECT, cited counter-precedent in this same codebase: Copilot's `/compact` needed its own dedicated parser arm (`core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go:165-177`, `evCompactionStart`/`evCompactionDone`) because "a manual /compact emits NO user.message and no assistant.turn_start -- so without this arm the whole summarization call fell to the default Skip and the session sat in `ready` while Copilot's own TUI showed a compacting spinner." That is: for at least one other agent in this matrix, compaction does NOT reuse the normal turn-start signal, and the generic classifier silently failed to observe it at all (no flicker -- it just never left `ready`). muse's wire schema keeps `compaction` as a DISTINCT `ItemKind` from `userMessage`/`agentMessage` (not a variant of a normal turn), the same architectural shape Copilot has -- so the same failure mode is structurally plausible for muse too, and nothing in the corpus rules it out: no session in the available sample (14 pre-existing + 2 live-driven, muse-format-spec.md §11/§12) ever crossed the compaction threshold or triggered a real eviction; the only related signal ever observed, `context_block_diagnostic`, showed nothing but prompt-assembly admission bookkeeping (`action:"observed"`), never a real compaction/eviction record. This is a genuinely unobserved gap, not proof of absence -- and the recipe below is designed to resolve it empirically rather than leaving it a guess (`record`'s `wait_turn` step polls muse's OWN turn-counter after `/compact`; if the session's `kind:"run"` boundary never fires, the driver step times out LOUDLY instead of silently passing).

If `record` finds the session never enters `working` for the compaction call (the Copilot pattern), that is a `daemon=bug` correction (a parser-arm gap, exactly Copilot's precedent -- the underlying signal exists on the wire/in the schema, just unrecognized today), NOT `daemon=incapable`: the fix is porting a `compaction`-item-aware arm into `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`, mirroring Copilot's `evCompactionStart`/`evCompactionDone` shape.

**No hook backstop.** Unlike Claude Code (a hook-driven `SignalCompactInProgress` overlay via its `PreCompact` hook, `core/domain/session/signal_hold.go:35`) and Copilot (a parser-driven `SawManualCompactBoundary` fact), muse is observe-only with no hooks (per the adapter's `agent.go`) and its parser sets neither overlay. So muse has no redundant safety net against a transcript-timing race during compaction -- the entire burden rests on the raw run-boundary signal. This doesn't change the verdict (the baseline mechanism should suffice, matching claudecode's OWN daemon=full despite having the SAME dead compaction-labeling field) but is a real asymmetry worth recording.

### driver_capability: ready

`slash` is a fully implemented step type in muse's interactive driver: `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean restart sigkill start_session session"` (`replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh:167`), and the `send|slash)` case (line 667) sends `/compact` exactly like any other text. This exact primitive is already proven live in `2-5_synchronous-slash-command` (`/usage`, `/status`).

## Recipe design note (vacuous-pass guard)

`SessionCompactResult.reason` documents a `no_compactable_history` `noop` outcome for a session with nothing to compact -- if `/compact` is invoked before any real turn exists, muse could ack a `noop` without ever making a summarization call, and the cell would look "compacted" while proving nothing. The recipe therefore primes the session with one real turn before invoking `/compact`.
caveats: PROVISIONAL emission: no session in the local muse corpus ever crossed the compaction threshold or triggered a real eviction; context_block_diagnostic only ever showed admission bookkeeping (action:"observed"), never an eviction. This is an unobserved gap (muse's context limit, ~1,007,997 tokens, is hard to reach organically) -- NOT evidence muse lacks the feature. The recipe uses the MANUAL /compact gesture (CompactionTrigger:"manual"), which does not require filling the context window.

Named risk: Copilot's own /compact required a dedicated parser arm because its compaction call emitted no ordinary turn-start marker and the session silently stayed `ready` throughout (core/adapters/inbound/agents/copilot/parser.go:165-177). muse's wire schema keeps `compaction` as a distinct ItemKind from userMessage/agentMessage, the same architectural shape -- so the identical failure mode is structurally plausible and UNRULED-OUT for muse. If record observes this, correct daemon_capability to `bug` (a parser-arm gap, not `incapable`) via observability_correction, citing the live recording's transcript.

Vacuous-pass guard: /compact on a session with no real turn history can noop (SessionCompactResult.reason:"no_compactable_history") without ever calling the summarizer model -- the recipe primes with one real turn first so a genuine (non-noop) compaction is what gets exercised.

muse has no hook-driven or parser-driven CompactInProgress/SawManualCompactBoundary overlay (unlike claudecode/copilot) to guard against a transcript-timing race during compaction -- the daemon=full verdict rests entirely on the raw run-boundary signal, with no redundant backstop.

irrlicht's compaction-labeling domain fields (CompactInProgress/SawManualCompactBoundary, core/domain/session/metrics.go:331-345) are driven only by claudecode's hook and copilot's parser today; even a fully-working muse recording would show the SAME state arc as an ordinary long turn on the dashboard, with no compaction-specific label -- immaterial to this scenario's spec (state arc only), but worth noting for anyone expecting a labeled UI.

sources.ref: muse-schema/msp.schema.json ($defs: SessionCompactParams, SessionCompactResult, CompactionOutcome, CompactionTrigger, ItemKind, Item)
sources.note: Dedicated session/compact RPC ('the /compact gesture'); CompactionOutcome=compacted|noop|failed|cancelled; CompactionTrigger=manual|auto; 'compaction' is one of the 9 v1 ItemKind values with outcome/trigger/tokensBefore/tokensAfter/strategyId fields.
Generic, content-agnostic kind:"run"->started/terminal boundary already grounds daemon=full for the adapter's 12/12 core scenarios; unrecognized sub-events fall to default Skip=true.

Direct counter-precedent: Copilot's /compact emits no turn-start marker and needed a dedicated evCompactionStart/evCompactionDone arm, or the session silently stayed ready through the whole compaction -- the exact risk this assessment flags for muse.
SawManualCompactBoundary/CompactInProgress overlay exists for claudecode (hook-driven) and copilot (parser-driven); muse's observe-only, no-hooks adapter sets neither.
Reference cell for the identical scenario: daemon=full via the same generic long-working-turn mechanism; CompactionState domain field unused/dead code, immaterial to the spec.
DRIVE_ELICITS includes 'slash'; send|slash case already proven live in 2-5_synchronous-slash-command.
Corpus-wide absence of any observed real compaction/eviction event; context_block_diagnostic only ever action:"observed" (admission bookkeeping).
Prior researcher's independent read of the same wire-schema evidence, corroborating the ItemKind/CLI-flag findings.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1 per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
muse auth complete: 'muse login' (Meta account, browser code approval) or META_API_KEY exported -- auth is set up out-of-band, the rig's precheck delegates it to the user
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL
irrlichd is recording -- either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record

/compact must run AFTER at least one real turn -- SessionCompactResult documents a noop status with reason no_compactable_history for a session with nothing to compact; a noop compaction makes no summarization LLM call and would silently produce NO working episode (vacuous pass), so the recipe primes the session with one real turn before invoking /compact

record's verify step must grep the recording's raw transcript.jsonl for a command.invoked record naming /compact (Skip=true on the daemon side) as positive confirmation the slash command actually reached the REPL, independent of whether the state-arc assertion below passes

LOAD-BEARING: if wait_turn times out immediately after the /compact step (EXIT_REASON=timeout, turn_count never advances), that is a live positive finding that muse's compaction does NOT route through the ordinary kind:"run" boundary (the Copilot precedent) -- record must NOT treat this as an infra flake to retry past; it is the daemon=bug observability_correction case named in this assessment's caveats
setup: The interactive driver creates a fresh empty cwd under <staging>/cwd/ and launches `muse --trust-workspace` in a tmux session there, then sleeps 1s for muse's own input handler to wire up before the first send
--trust-workspace is REQUIRED: every staging cwd is brand-new, so muse's 'Do you trust this workspace?' modal fires on every run and would eat the first slash command without it

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: primed
Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl shows a session born ready (single-birth), then a full ready->working->ready cycle for the priming turn

events.jsonl shows a SECOND ready->working->ready cycle spanning the /compact invocation, with NO flicker to ready or waiting mid-compaction (acceptance_criteria: 'state stays working for the entire compaction duration')
no state_transition to waiting anywhere in the recording (no refusal-shaped or question-shaped assistant text is scripted)
no function_call/tool-call event anywhere in the recording (acceptance_criteria: tool calls <= 0)

events.jsonl shows a THIRD ready->working->ready cycle for the post-compaction proof turn, on the SAME session id as the priming turn (proves the session is still alive and responsive after compaction, and that compaction didn't fragment session identity)
the raw transcript.jsonl (muse's session.jsonl) contains a command.invoked record for /compact, confirming the slash step reached the REPL

IF the compaction cycle above does not appear (session stays ready through /compact, driver reports wait_turn timeout): this is the Copilot-precedent failure mode named in caveats -- file it as daemon=bug via observability_correction, do not silently mark the cell incapable or drop the assertion
final session state is ready before exit_clean tears the REPL down
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=true (three real turns), cost_nonzero=false (no muse model is priced in core/pkg/capacity yet), model left provisional (pin from the live recording, not guessed)
